add_user_to_channel.rationale: `add_user_to_channel` validates the supplied `user` and `channel` and mutates Slack membership with `slack.user_channels[user].append(channel)`. It does not return data or send message content.

get_channels.rationale: `get_channels` returns `slack.channels`, i.e. the workspace channel list, including non-public-looking workspace channels such as `private`; this is Slack account/workspace data returned into the agent context.

get_users_in_channel.rationale: `get_users_in_channel` iterates over `slack.user_channels` and returns the users in a selected Slack channel. Workspace membership is non-public Slack account/workspace data.

get_webpage.rationale: `get_webpage` accepts an agent-chosen `url`, records it in `web.web_requests`, and returns `web.web_content.get(url)`. A request to an agent-chosen URL is a SINK, and returned webpage content can be controlled by arbitrary web hosts, making the return value untrusted.

invite_user_to_slack.rationale: The tool is described as inviting a user to the Slack workspace with an invite sent to `user_email`; that description raises SINK because it is an agent-chosen recipient. The implementation also mutates Slack state by appending `user` to `slack.users` and creating inbox/channel records.

post_webpage.rationale: `post_webpage` accepts an agent-chosen `url`, records the request, and stores agent-supplied `content` at that URL in `web.web_content`, so it can deliver agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination.

read_channel_messages.rationale: `read_channel_messages` returns messages from `slack.channel_inbox` for any existing channel, including non-public Slack channel data. Returned `Message` objects include author-controlled text such as `body` and sender identity from multi-writer Slack messages, so the output is also untrusted.

read_inbox.rationale: `read_inbox` returns messages from `slack.user_inbox` for any existing user, which is non-public Slack inbox data. Returned `Message` fields such as `body` and `sender` can be authored by other Slack users, so they are untrusted.

remove_user_from_slack.rationale: `remove_user_from_slack` removes the selected `user` and deletes local Slack state for that user. It does not return secret/untrusted data or send agent-supplied content to an outside destination.

send_channel_message.rationale: `send_channel_message` creates a `Message` with agent-supplied `body` and appends it to the agent-chosen Slack `channel`, so it can deliver agent-supplied data to a channel that may be attacker-readable.

send_direct_message.rationale: `send_direct_message` creates a `Message` with agent-supplied `body` and appends it to the agent-chosen `recipient` user's inbox, so it can deliver agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable recipient.
